links.reason: Both name killing and flesh-eating as hell's sins (அட்டு உயிர் உடலம் தின்றான் / கொன்ற பாவம், தின்ற பாவம்), but Neelakesi 97 never names regicide or any political crime. Nothing is developed; the claim that the minor epic's catalogue holds the regicide is false.

1867 says festival-goers gain a heavenly form (விண்ணியல் உருவம் எய்தி); 1882 says in hearsay (என்பவே) that deeds sweated and died. Making the one feed the other as a karma ledger is the note's inference; the verses do not join them.
கணிபுகழ் காளை in 722 can mean the youth the astrologers praise, but 539 foretells only a husband in Rajamapuram, not the lute contest. 'Prophecy fulfilled' is the marker's inference from one epithet.

The nun says penance is hard (அருந்தவம் அரிது) and the gift yields fame then heaven, which does qualify Kural 47's primacy of the householder. But 'அரிது' is hard, not higher, and the gains clauses (a rival ranking; the couplet answered by fame and heaven) are strained.

Arisenan's boast offers the foe a chance to retreat (மறிமின்); it is not shown as a quest for fame over life as in கழல்யாப்பு. The teaches rests on 1294 which is not the linked verse, and the note's 'among the first to fall' is unsupported.

838's host is the Rathanupuram king's, likened to a sea (கடலோடொக்கும் சேனை); 949's hosts are rivers meeting (கங்கைபோற் ... யமுனையின்). Sea and river are different images, and that the host is the same one is an unproved identification.
links.text_issue: 949 sense flagged uncertain; whose hosts is inferred.

links.reason: Neelakesi 222 mocks the self-offering of a monkey lying with outstretched tail; Kundalakesi 1 praises one who laboured only for others (பிறர்க்கே உறுதிக்கு உழந்தான்) without naming any tale. The opposition of self-offering and result is real but the pairing needs the Jataka identification, and the invocation never claims profit-less sacrifice.
Draws the sword (கையில்வாள் உருவினானே) in 58, puts it aside (தன்கை வாளும் ... மாற்றி) in 67: a reversal. The sword is incidental, so same_image is the wrong type; develops fits.

Naladiyar 57 praises those who hold vows against troubles; 148 says only that hunger-pain came on the fast day (இடர்பசி ஆயிற்று). It does not show holding firm or death, so the 'extreme case' claim goes beyond the verse.
Both undo the body's finery with a trifling hurt (சிறுமுள் தீண்ட ... / ஈச்சிறகு அன்னது ஓர் தோல் அற). But the epic has no crows; the 'gain' to the epic side is invented.

The verse is damaged (three lines, first word lost), and its last line says he cooled 'such is his nature' (ஆயபண்பு), which fits the quatrain rather than qualifying it. 'Cools only after kin speak' leans on the damaged text.

1977 adds that those of faultless human form but cruel livelihood (கொடுந்தொழில் வாழ்க்கையர்) are base; 1973 already calls them குமானுடர். A modest extension within one passage whose middle verses carry the marks; thin.

If one makes fire for food and does harm, deeds cast him into burning flame (வெந்தெரியுள் வீழுமே), an instance of Kural 320's return of pain. The verse's first lines are obscure, and the pairing only illustrates the law.
1762 gives the drum order (முரசம் ... அறைக) and 1763 the drum struck (அதிர்ந்து அறைந்தவே). It is plot order, which the graph already records; nothing is answered or reversed.

Tirumanthiram 165 sends those who do not worship the form to the seventh hell; 1951 begins a list of adulterers falling into hell. Different criteria for different sins are not incompatible claims, and what the sage's later verses omit is not in the packet.
374 says wealth and wisdom are separate fates (திருவேறு தெள்ளியராதலும் வேறு); 400 calls learning the wealth (கேடில் விழுச்செல்வம் கல்வி). The pairing 'redefines wealth' is only the shared theme.

167 says her eyes madden even sages (முனிவரையும் மால் உறுப்ப); 181 has the king caught in the net of her long eyes (நெடுந்தடங்கண் வலைப்பட்டு). A real fulfilment, but 'the first one captured' is not in the text and 181's sense is flagged.

Both use a lamp on a hill (கார்த்திகை விளக்கு இட்டு அன்ன ... / குன்றத்து உச்சிச் சுடர்ப் பழி விளக்கு), a real echo. But 256's simile is of Madanan's sweating chest, not flattery, so 'passes from praise to blame' is false.

27:277-278 has her say of all the paths 'நன்று அல' and still hear them; 26:65-66 sets hearing each school until its lack of truth is plain (மெய் வகை இன்மை நினக்கே விளங்கிய பின்னர்) before the Buddha's path. The debate chapter does carry out the prescribed course.

The simile (உணர்வின் மிக்கான் ஒழித்திடப் பெயர்ந்ததேபோல்) does grant the heart goes out first, a mild qualification of Kural 148's 'நோக்காத'. But it is an incidental simile mocking the king, and the gains clauses ('second chance') are the marker's gloss.

115: they do not pick up fallen jewels (எடுத்துக் கொள்ளா ஒழுக்கினர்); Sil 5:111-117: bundles lie unguarded because a thief is made to bear his load on his head and whirl (தலைஏற்றிக் கொட்பின்). The contrast is real, but the lines name no spirit, and 'qualifies' does not fit two city descriptions.

The idyll's simile has birds seeking fruiting trees (பழுமரம் தேரும் பறவை போல) for the bard seeking a patron; Kural 216 has a fruit tree in the town (உள்ளூர்ப் பழுத்தற்று). The shared figure is real, but within 1-22 the tree is not yet the patron, and the 'guide poem exists because' clause is an overreach.

2906 (அறத்தை ஓம்பின் ... இன்பம் இல்லை) praises the unbent sceptre (கோல் வளையாமல்), echoing Kural 546's கோல் கோடாது, but not in words. Giving the Kural's victory to the epic is the note's addition, not a gain.

253 files killing and flesh-eating with sins that send to hell (அட்டு உயிர் உடலம் தின்றான்); 2776 adds those who deny the next world and the soul (இம்மை அல்லால் உம்மையும் உயிரும் என்பார்) as going the same way. The refuted view is rightly given as the teacher's account, and the extension to belief is real.

819 shows Padumukan tending the wounded with ghee and cloths; 2353 asks that the men with wounds be tended (புண்கொண்டு போற்றி). The 'uncle' and 'first order as king' of the note are not in the verse, and the pair is a repeated motif.

Prithidevi's fear is her own supposition (காண்டற்கு நின்றாள் என்று), and the verse shows no envy. The Silappathikaram lines list a woman who raised a co-wife's child; nothing in them contradicts the fear, so there is no tension.

198 says only that the speaker acted by force against the treatises (நூல் நெறியின் நின்றி வன்மையாற் சூழ்ச்சி செய்தேன்); the plot is not named, and 129 in this very packet suggests a stratagem of parting the king from his queen, not the guise of 109.

140 names one flaw, அருளாமை toward lower lives (கீழுயிர்), among virtues; Kural 557 compares lack of அளி to rain's lack. The verse names the flaw but does not show it undoing the rest, so nothing is 'tested'.

251: if he says sending the king to heaven and ruling the earth is good, that is not clean (வாலிது அன்று); 259: let the king go to rule heaven (மன்னன் போய்த் துறக்கம் ஆண்டு) while I guard the earth. The foreseen pretext is then used. 'Trap' is rhetorical.
Both show battlefield pey-women (பேய் மகளிர் ... துணங்கை / சூற்பேய் ஆட), but 803 shows a toilette watched by Civakan, and the king-performed rite and the 'later descent' are not in either text.

155 charges that the king threw a living-shaped offering to the goddess (சேதன வடிவு தேவிக்கு எறிந்தனன்) and so this has come (ஆதலால் வந்தது இன்று); 145 shows him cutting the flour cock (தன்கை வாளால் அரிந்து). A mourners' reading of cause, rightly marked as reported.
104 holds only the king's question; the answer is in 105, and 109 says the brothers hear the account (என்றவர் உரையைக் கேட்டு) and become servants. 'Foresight exact' needs the unseen verse.

Both turn on a hunger filled as a mountain fills the sea (பெருங் கடல் வெள்ளிக் குன்றம் பெய்து தூர்க்கின்ற / நெடு மலை எல்லாம் ... அளக்கர் வயிறு புக்காங்கு), a real shared image. But 400 does not name the disease, the 'Jain household' is not in it, and the Jain/Buddhist contrast is added.

147 asks if sin calls him to the garland of births (பிறவி மாலை); 161 announces only that the king and mother died attached and births will be told (பல்பிறப்பு உரைக்குறுகின்றதே). The account is not in 161; this is a pointer, not a fulfilment.
1416 is about Kanaka Naman (கனக நாமனே); 1417 shows Kanaka Chitran (கனகசித் திரனும்) struck by the plough tip. They are different men, so the 'he is struck down' of the note misreads 1417.

482 argues lineage is no bar, citing Murukan and Valli; 483 holds that a man should not take an unequal wife before one of his rank (குலத்தின் மிக்கார் ... முன்). Orders rather than denies it, so a qualification, not a clash.

323's 'செங்கண்மான்' is Tirumal in heaven (விண்மேல் செங்கண்மான்); 2 names the hero as செங்கண் நெடியான். Joining them by an epithet and calling a counsellor's boast a tension with the proem is a stretch.

1597: the brahmin cries out that a spirit strikes and eats (பூதம் உண்டு அதுபுடைத்து உண்ணும்). Kural 428 says not fearing what is to be feared is folly; the shadow revelation is not in 1597, so the 'misplaced fear' qualifier rests on later verses. Illustration.

1283 boasts (யான் அவ்வரிசேனன் ... உயிர் வாழலுறின்); 1294 shows Arisenan cut in two (மார்பம் இரு போழாய்). The scene undoes the boast, but this is a reversal, not incompatible claims; develops fits better.

Death as a woman is shared (கூற்றென்பதனை இனி அறிந்தேன், பெண்டகை / கோமகள் உருவமாய்க் கூற்றம் போந்தது); the contrast of private discovery with public warning is true. That is a same_image, and the 'gains' about a source and about the couplet gaining a scene are not real.

124 has the poet blame the king who forgets the lost land (இழந்ததன் நிலத்தையும் ... நினைத்திலன்); 129 has Yugi, hearing this (இழந்த பூமி எண்ணிலன்), plan to part him from the queen to recover it. The plan answers the neglect, not just follows it.

The pairing puts heaven as reward (சீலம் ... கப்பத்து அமரர் ஆவர்) beside the claim that heaven's dwellers renounce nothing (என்னதும் துறவலர்), so heaven is shown as no end. A real qualification, in Jain terms.

The kings who rose and fled (புறக்கிட்டு ஓடினார்) are an instance of Kural 473's broken-midway. But the epic names no cause, and the 'rising without knowing their strength' is the Kural's cause put into the epic, not a gain.
